text:
maia-docs: FYI opened a docs PR that covers an IPsec (strongSwan) tunnel option for private/on-prem installs where WireGuard isn't allowed by policy. Includes packaging notes for .deb vs .rpm and an offline-mirror checklist. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/8210 :sparkles:

ruz-infra: Nice. Can you paste the minimal strongSwan conn config you used? customers usually want the quick example for IKEv2 + RSA certs.

maia-docs: Pasted in PR and here: 
```
# /etc/ipsec.d/roadwarrior.conf
conn redwood-site
  keyexchange=ikev2
  auto=add
  left=%defaultroute
  leftcert=site.crt
  right=redwood-gw.example.internal
  rightsubnet=10.50.0.0/16
  ike=aes256gcm16-prfsha384-modp2048
  esp=aes256gcm16
```

devon-packaging: Quick note for packaging: the dpkg install on Debian 11 requires pacemaker if using advanced cluster helpers; we should not mention pacemaker unless customers run HA. For RPM (RHEL8+) add `--nodocs` rpm example for minimal installs. I'll add distro-specific commands.

maia-docs: Added snippets for apt and yum: `apt-get install strongswan` and `yum install strongswan` plus `yumdownloader --destdir=/tmp strongswan` for offline mirror downloads. Also included `apt-offline` pointers.

olga-qa: QA checklist - please include tests for the tunnel bringing up the interface after package upgrade. I hit a case where systemd restarted before certs were present and strongswan failed. Recommend a systemd unit override snippet to make strongswan wait for /etc/redwood/certs to be present.

maia-docs: Good catch. Added `systemctl edit strongswan.service` snippet with `After=network-online.target local-fs.target` and a `RequiresMountsFor=/etc/redwood/certs` line.

sam-ux: UX nit: in the offline mirror section, show the exact `sha512sum` command and how to verify against the signed manifest. Many ops teams ask for sha512 vs sha256.

maia-docs: Done. Added: `sha512sum redwood-offline-bundle-2.0.0.tar.gz` and a note: "compare against MANIFEST.sha512 (signed) and verify signature with `gpg --verify` using our public key."

devon-packaging: HSM/PKCS11 note: some customers using YubiHSM2 hit a PUK/PUK retry confusion if they factory-reset tokens during install. We should document the `yubihsm-shell` commands to check device status and the installer behaviour if token needs re-init.

maia-docs: I added a caution: "Do not reset YubiHSM tokens during installer run. If a token is reset, re-run the `redwood-installer --repair-hsm` flow and re-import keys. Example pkcs11 path: `/usr/lib64/libyubihsm.so`". Also included `yubihsm-shell list` example.

olga-qa: Also add `softhsm2` unit test steps: `softhsm2-util init-token --free` and how to populate a test key so QA can smoke the PKCS#11 path without hardware.

maia-docs: Added the SoftHSM init example and a tiny snippet for `pkcs11-tool --module /usr/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so --list-slots`.

ruz-infra: For customers behind strict egress, include an `apt-mirror` recipe for Debian packages and an `reposync` example for RHEL repos. Also show how to sign local repo metadata and configure `repos.d` entries in the installer.

maia-docs: Added `apt-mirror` config sample and `reposync --download-metadata` example. Also a note: when mirroring, increment `MaxAge` in our repo metadata or use a short TTL to prevent stale packages during staged deploys.

sam-ux: One more UX thing: add a short table of which ciphers we recommend (no CBC, prefer GCM). People search for "supported ciphers" a lot.

maia-docs: Added a recommended ciphers section: `ike: aes256gcm16-prfsha384-modp2048` and `esp: aes256gcm16`. Included a short line about FIPS mode differences.

deploy-bot: build-docs: success (sha: d4e5f6a) - preview deployed to https://docs-preview.internal/6113334444

olga-qa: I'll run the smoke tomorrow and post any failures here. If anyone wants to add quick follow-ups, ping me.

devon-packaging: I'll add the dpkg/rpm samples in the packaging repo and link them from the PR.

maia-docs: Thanks all 49b3fb Will push a small wording update after QA.
